name: Montgomery & Selma
summary: The cradle of the Confederacy and of the civil-rights movement — Rosa Parks, Dr. King's church, the Legacy sites, and the Selma bridge.

lodging.name: A downtown Montgomery hotel
lodging.blurb: Walkable to the Capitol and the civil-rights sites.

days.label: Day 279 — Montgomery
days.summary: The movement's beginnings and a searing memorial.

item.title: The Legacy Museum & National Memorial for Peace and Justice

location.name: National Memorial for Peace and Justice

item.blurb: EJI's unflinching museum of slavery-to-mass-incarceration and the memorial to lynching victims — profoundly moving.

item.title: Rosa Parks Museum & Dexter Ave Church
item.blurb: Where the bus boycott began, plus Dr. King's Dexter Avenue church and the Alabama Capitol up the hill.

days.label: Day 280 — Selma
days.summary: The bridge that changed voting rights.

item.title: Edmund Pettus Bridge & Voting Rights Museum
item.blurb: Walk the bridge where marchers were beaten on 'Bloody Sunday' in 1965, and the National Voting Rights Museum at its foot.

rest.label: The rest of today is deliberately empty
rest.note: The Legacy Museum, the National Memorial for Peace and Justice, Montgomery, and now the Edmund Pettus Bridge — four days of the hardest and most important material on this itinerary, one after another with nothing between them. Nothing is scheduled after Selma. Walk the bridge a second time if you want to. Otherwise sit down somewhere and let it land.

commute.scenicNote: Northeast into Tennessee and the mountains.
